# S295 — Check command: verify it once where it will run, at projects set and at run setup

*Proposed.* ork verifies a project's check command where it will run, before anything depends on it: when the owner sets it with `ork projects set --check`, and at run or wave setup before the implementer starts. The verification is cheap and bounded (it runs nothing but `sh -n`): the first word resolves, and the files the command names exist in the directory the check will use. A failure is reported with the command and the directory, as a refusal at `projects set` and as a pause before round 1 at setup. Owner decisions, 2026-11-05: the static tier only, nothing executes; a failure at run or wave setup pauses that run while the rest of the wave goes on, and the run continues after the fix (see below); a named-file miss at `projects set` is refused, with `--no-verify` to store it anyway.

Owner decision, 2026-11-05 (option (a) of the former Q1): to fix a check command that failed verification at setup, the owner stops the run (`ork stop ID`), sets the check (`ork projects set PROJECT --check CMD`), then runs `ork retry ID`, which resumes the stopped run through S296. This slice therefore depends on S296, whose resume enters `implement` (not `checks`) when no implementer round has run. The setup pause reason names those three commands.

**Findings:** 2026-11-05, prism-ui: both check commands the owner set (dotnet build PrismUi.slnx ...) were wrong from the worktree root, and nothing noticed until U41 and U30 burned 8 rounds each on MSB1009. Wanted: at run or wave setup and in 'ork projects set --check', verify the command in the exact directory the check will use and say so, with the command and directory, before any role starts. Bounded cost: a full check at setup is too slow. ork doctor already parses with sh -n and resolves the first word (internal/cli/doctor.go:171-210), but only for the main checkout and not the files the command names. Not S293 (which directory); this validates it. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-05** — [decision] Owner decision 2026-11-05 (interactive interview), Q1 option (a): to fix a check command that failed verification at setup, stop the run, run ork projects set --check, then ork retry ID, which resumes the stopped run through S296. S295 depends on S296; S296's resume enters implement when no implementer round has run.

**Not in this slice:** which directory the check runs in (S293; this slice validates whatever directory the round check uses); running the full check at setup (owner declined 2026-11-05); presets, allowlists and the no-check-command warning (S265); the busy rule of `projects set` (S265 Q5); the round pause when a check cannot pass (S294); resuming a stopped run, which the fix path uses (S296, a dependency).

## Why

Owner evidence, 2026-11-05 (prism-ui, a project in a subfolder of its repo): both check commands the owner set (`dotnet build PrismUi.slnx ...`) were wrong from the worktree root, and nothing noticed until two runs (U41 and U30) burned 8 rounds each on `MSB1009: Project file does not exist` (see S294 for the run records). S293 makes the check run from the project's folder; this slice makes ork notice a check that cannot run before a role is spent on it.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-05):

- The check runs as `sh -c COMMAND` in `rec.Worktree` (`RunCheck`, `internal/engine/check.go:19-33`; called from `runChecks`, `internal/engine/states.go:191-213`). The worktree is `.worktrees/{id}` under the project path by default (`worktreePath`, `internal/engine/engine.go:140-150`) and is a full checkout of the repo, so its root is the repo root, not the project's subfolder. A check that works from `p.Path` can fail from the worktree root: that is the evidence case and S293's subject.
- `ork projects set --check` stores the string with no check (`setProject`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:528-637`; flags at `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:278` and the list at `:356`). It refuses every field while the project has an unfinished run (`handlers.go:587-593`); a paused run is unfinished (`runrec.IsFinal`, `internal/runrec/record.go:39`). S265's Q5 answer (2026-11-03) lets only the cap, budgets and patterns through, so `--check` stays refused while a run is paused. A started engine also keeps the project it started with (`internal/daemon/runs.go:578-579`).
- `ork doctor` already has the static tier for the main checkout: `checkProject` (`internal/cli/doctor.go:173-221`) runs `sh -n -c` (`:185`) (parse only, "even substitutions and redirects must never execute") and resolves the first word with `checkCommandWord` (`doctor.go:99`) and `exec.LookPath`, relative words against `p.Path`. (`checkCommandWord` is `doctor.go:99-150`.) It does not look at the other words of the command, and it checks `p.Path`, not the directory the round check uses.
- Setup (`setup`, `internal/engine/states.go:25-46`) creates the worktree and the ledger run, then moves to `implement`. Its comment says a setup failure stops the slice because "nothing was started that a retry could take over"; a retry that re-entered `setup` would call `RelayBegin` again. Nothing looks at the check command until `checks` after round 1.
- A setup failure today stops the run (`states.go:30-34`); a tool failure in `runChecks` pauses with `PendingError` (`states.go:202-213`).
- Cost: the full checks are slow (slicer's suite 8 to 16 minutes, S265 note of 2026-11-03; the check timeout is 10 minutes unless the project sets one, `internal/engine/states.go:198-201`), so a full check at setup would double the cheapest run's check time.

Owner decision, 2026-11-05 (option (a) of the former Q1): the busy rule and the engine's copy of the project (above) mean that `ork projects set --check` then a plain `ork retry ID` cannot fix the check while the run is paused. So the fix path is: `ork stop ID` (a stopped run is final and does not block `projects set`, S296 Why), `ork projects set PROJECT --check CMD`, then `ork retry ID`, which resumes the stopped run with the project as it is now (S296). The busy rule stays as S265 decided. A plain `ork retry ID` at the pause still re-verifies with the started engine's check, which helps only when the fix is a file added in the worktree.

Not verified: that every MSB-style "missing file" error is caught by the static file check (it catches it only when the file is named on the command line, as `PrismUi.slnx` was).

## Failing tests

In `internal/engine/check_test.go` (table tests, temp directories):

- `TestVerifyCheckMissingNamedFile`: `dotnet build App.slnx -c Release` in a directory without `App.slnx` returns one problem naming `App.slnx`, the directory and the command. With `sub/App.slnx` and dir `sub` it returns none. Fails first: no `VerifyCheck`.
- `TestVerifyCheckFirstWordNotFound`: `nosuchtool test` returns "not found on PATH"; `./run-tests.sh` missing returns "not found in DIR".
- `TestVerifyCheckIgnoresFlagsGlobsAndModules`: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test*.py'`, `go test ./...`, `python3 -m unittest tests.test_x` return no problem (flags, globs, `./...` and dotted module names are not file names). Guard against false positives.
- `TestVerifyCheckRunsNothing`: a command `touch MARK && false` leaves no `MARK` (only `sh -n` runs).

In `internal/engine/engine_test.go`: `TestSetupPausesWhenTheCheckCannotRun` (a check naming a missing file pauses before round 1 with the command and the directory in the reason; no implementer role ran; a retry with the file still missing pauses again, and with the file present runs round 1; `RelayBegin` was called once). The pause reason names `ork stop ID`, `ork projects set` and `ork retry ID`. Fails first: round 1 runs.

In `internal/engine/engine_test.go` (needs S296): `TestSetupPauseFixedByStopSetAndRetry`: a check naming a missing file pauses at setup; the owner stops the run, the project's check changes to one that verifies, and the S296 resume runs `VerifyCheck` with the new command, then implementer round 1 (not `checks`); `RelayBegin` was called twice (S296 begins a new ledger run). Fails first: the resume is refused or enters `checks`.

In `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go`: `TestProjectsSetCheckRefusesAMissingFile` (refusal names file and directory; `--no-verify` stores it), `TestProjectsSetCheckVerifiesWhereTheRoundCheckRuns` (a project in `sub/` of its repo: the directory verified is the one the round check uses, not `p.Path`). Fails first: stored without a check.

## Implement

1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. Add `engine.VerifyCheck(ctx, dir, command)`: `sh -n -c` (no execution); the first word of each simple command resolves (`LookPath`, relative words against `dir`); each later word that is a plain path (has a `/` or a file extension of letters after its last `.`, no glob or `$`, not starting with `-`, not `./...`) and is followed by no redirect must exist under `dir`. Dotted names without an extension of letters only and words after `-m` are skipped. Return one-line problems.
3. One helper gives the check directory for a worktree (today `rec.Worktree`; S293 changes it). If S293 lands first and adds such a helper, reuse it. Use it in `runChecks`, in setup verification and, mapped to the main checkout, in `setProject`.
4. `setup`: after the worktree and the ledger run exist, run `VerifyCheck`; on a problem pause (`PendingError`, `pending.state` `implement`, so a retry does not repeat `RelayBegin`) with `check command cannot run in DIR: PROBLEM (command: CMD)` followed by `; to fix the check: ork stop ID, ork projects set PROJECT --check CMD, then ork retry ID` (owner decision 2026-11-05; `ork projects set` is refused while this run is paused, so the run is stopped first). `implement` runs `VerifyCheck` again before round 1 when no implementer round has run and it was entered from a retry of this pause or from an S296 resume, and pauses again on a problem.
5. `setProject`: verify a changed `--check` unless `--no-verify`; refuse with the same one line.
6. The resume of the stopped run is S296's (this slice depends on it): S296 reloads the project from the registry, records the paused run's `pending.state` (`implement`) as `stopped_from`, begins a new ledger run and enters `implement` because no implementer round has run. This slice adds no resume code.
7. `planRun`: add the problem to the plan so the launch shows it.
8. `doctor`: use the shared function; keep its finding texts.
9. Docs and CHANGELOG in the same diff.
